structure: Part 1, shared layout, copy and page kit. Read in full: src/server/app/routes.js and features/index.js (route composition); shared/layout.njk (GOV.UK template with header, service navigation, phase banner, maturity banner include, back link, recoverable-error banner, journey strip, two-thirds or full content column, footer); shared/error.njk and error-summary.njk; shared/copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js and copy-leaves.js (locale resolution, the shared chrome copy and validator default messages in English and machine-draft Welsh); shared/kit.js (base view model, surfaces, error summary model, draft journey strip, organisation guard, page route builder); shared/paths.js (every INS page path and the two section tests that drive the active navigation item); shared/list-page.js (page parsing, clamping, results label and pagination links); shared/escape-html.js; page-maturity/banner.njk, levels.js, page-maturity.js and its en/cy copy (four maturity levels shown as a second phase banner); app/auth/page.js and the four sign-in templates (unauthorised and the three hidden IDM test pages); src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js (view context: nav urls, active item, user session, crumb, maturity); the fit specs features/page-title.fit.spec.js (9 tests) and fit/smoke.fit.spec.js (1 test) and the fit helpers fit/error-focus.js and fit/axe.js; and the repo's notes docs/README.md (served route list), architecture.md (chassis and application split, error and auth pages, templates, client assets, enforced boundaries, how INS differs from the journey frontends), features.md (feature shapes, paths, page kit, controller shape, copy and templates, validation, client JavaScript, the temporary address-lookup spike, tests) and services.md (barrel/client/stub shape, run mode, each service's contract, configuration, out of scope). Claims cover the chrome every page shares, every shared copy string with its Welsh twin, every path builder, the paging helper, the maturity levels, the sign-in templates, every test in the two specs and the conventions the docs record, as existing rulings. Feature-specific detail the docs repeat for the address book's own pages (fields, roles, tabs, return-to) is left to the parts that own those pages.

Templates: extend `shared/layout.njk`, import macros at the top, fill the
`journeyContent` block, `{% include "shared/error-summary.njk" %}` above
the `<h1>`, a hidden `crumb` input in every form

claims.statement: Ruling: fields are rendered with GOV.UK macros and show their own error message beside the field.
claims.quote:
fields rendered with
govuk macros, `errorMessage: errors.field and { text: errors.field }`.

claims.statement: Ruling: a field's name, id and error key stay identical so the error summary link focuses the field.
claims.quote:
Input `name`, `id` and the error-map key stay identical so the summary
link focuses the control.

claims.statement: Ruling: pages stay inside the GOV.UK Frontend toolbox.
The service also loads the Ministry of Justice frontend, for its sub navigation component only.
claims.quote:
the
`@ministryofjustice/frontend` package root (the sub navigation
macro)

claims.statement: Ruling: each feature with a template owns English and Welsh copy files with the same keys, and every Welsh string must differ from its English one, with 'GOV.UK' the only allowed exception.
claims.quote:
`cy` must have the same paths, leaf
kinds and function arities as `en`, and every string leaf must differ from
its English counterpart unless listed in
`copy-parity.test.js`'s `IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST`, which holds one entry,
`shared:layout.govukSuffix`

claims.statement: Ruling: a copy entry is a non-empty string or a function that builds a string from values, such as an added banner naming the address.
claims.quote:
a leaf is a
non-empty string or a string-returning function (parameterised copy, for
example `successBanner.added(name)`)

claims.statement: Ruling: the shared chrome copy (layout, journey strip, unable to sign in, error summary, recoverable error, error page) and the default validation messages reach every page as shared copy.
claims.quote:
Shared
chrome copy (`layout`, `journeyStrip`, `unauthorised`, `errorSummary`,
`recoverableError`, `errorPage`) and `validatorDefaults` live in
[`shared/copy.en.js`](../shared/copy.en.js) and `copy.cy.js`, and reach
every view as `sharedCopy`.

claims.statement: Ruling: a form's POST honours Cancel, validates, calls the service, sets a success banner and redirects.
claims.quote:
POST reads `request.payload`, honours `cancel`, validates, calls the
  service, sets the success banner and redirects.

claims.statement: Ruling: when a service call fails, the page logs the failure once and shows itself again with status 500 and the recoverable error banner.
claims.quote:
A service failure logs
  once (`logger.error({ err, organisationId }, '…')`) and re-renders with
  `recoverableError: true` and status 500 — the layout renders the banner.

claims.statement: Ruling: when the address book refuses a save as invalid, the page shows the API's first message for each field against that field.
claims.quote:
A 400 from the address book re-renders with
  `mapApiErrorsToFormErrors(err.body)`.

claims.statement: Ruling: the service's own JavaScript only initialises the GOV.UK components; a page needing more adds its own named script bundle.
claims.quote:
initialises the govuk components. A
page needing more adds a named `entry` to `webpack.config.js` and loads it
with `getAssetPath('<entry>.js')`.

claims.statement: Ruling: a feature never imports a sibling feature, only the route composition imports features, shared and library code import no feature or service, and circular imports are forbidden.
claims.quote: - **`feature-isolation`** — a feature never imports a sibling feature.

claims.statement: INS has no notification set, journey, obligation model, page engine or page dispatch: navigation is its fixed route list.
claims.quote:
ins has no set and no journey: there is one flat `features/` directory,
  not a platform/set split.

claims.statement: Ruling: each upstream service has a barrel, a real HTTP client and an in-memory stub, and a feature imports only the barrel.
claims.quote:
A feature imports only the barrel, and nothing
imports any other file from outside its folder.

claims.statement: One switch, STUB_MODE, makes the service serve stub data and sign users in with its own stub session; it is refused in production.
claims.quote:
It is
one service-wide switch, `STUB_MODE`, which also decides how a trader signs
in

claims.statement: A reference-data outage does not stop the service starting, because nothing is loaded at boot.
claims.quote:
There is no
priming at boot, so a reference-data outage does not stop the server
starting

claims.statement: The service calls the address book with the signed-in user's organisation, which must always come from the session, because the address book relies on the caller for organisation scoping.
claims.quote:
it must
always come from the session
claims.note: Security-relevant: organisation scoping depends on this service. Stated in general terms only.

claims.statement: The address book client refuses a call with no organisation rather than sending an empty one, and the INS backend facade does the same.
claims.quote:
refuses a missing organisation rather than asking for
`undefined`

claims.statement: A save to the address book sends the address's roles and no address type; an address's type is worked out from its roles.
claims.quote: A save sends the address's `roles` and no address type.

claims.statement: The country list comes from reference-data's '/countries', is cached for the life of the process, and a failed load shows the shared error page with a 503 and retries on the next read.
claims.quote:
a failed load
leaves the cache unloaded so the next read retries, and rejects with
`Boom.serverUnavailable`, which `catchAll` renders as the shared error
page with a 503.

claims.statement: The dashboard lists the organisation's aggregated notifications from the INS backend, by page, sort and reference number.
claims.quote:
`listNotifications(organisationId, { page, sort, referenceNumber })` —
the aggregated notifications the dashboard lists.

claims.statement: The dashboard's row links leave INS for the animals frontend, which owns the notification a row represents.
claims.quote:
The dashboard's row links leave the service for the
animals frontend (`TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL`), which owns the
notification a row represents.

claims.statement: Choosing a type on the notification type question sends the user to the start of the animals or plants frontend, which creates the draft.
claims.quote:
Choosing a type on `/notification-type` leaves
the service too: the POST redirects to the start entry of the animals or
plants frontend

claims.statement: A live animals notification's origin page can open the notification type question with the notification's reference and type, and keeping that type returns to the notification's origin page instead of starting a new one.
claims.quote:
The question then shows that type chosen, and keeping it redirects to
that notification's origin page instead of the start entry.

claims.statement: The service's upstream URLs are set by environment: address book (TRADE_IMPORTS_ADDRESS_BOOK_URL), reference data (TRADE_IMPORTS_REFERENCE_DATA_URL), INS backend (TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_BACKEND_URL), animals frontend (TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL) and plants frontend (TRADE_IMPORTS_PLANTS_FRONTEND_URL).
claims.note: The animals and plants frontend URLs are browser-visible; the three API URLs are server-side.

claims.statement: The content security policy lets forms post to the journey frontends and to the browser-facing Defra ID origin, so a hand-over can pass through sign-in.
claims.quote:
The form-action also trusts the origin of the browser-facing Defra ID URL, so
a hand-over to a journey frontend can pass through sign-in.

claims.statement: INS does no document upload and publishes no events; the notification itself belongs to the journey frontend.
claims.quote:
There is no document upload, no outbox and no event publishing here. The
notification itself is owned by the journey frontend the dashboard links
to.

claims.statement: After sign-in the user is always returned to a path on this service.
claims.quote:
so the redirect after sign-in is always a
path on this service.

claims.statement: Outbound connections wait up to one second per address before trying the next, as the animals and plants frontends do.
claims.quote:
It raises Node's process-wide happy-eyeballs
connect attempt per address from 250ms to one second

claims.statement: Outside the page routes, the service serves '/health', its sign-in routes under '/auth/' and static files under '/public/'.
claims.quote:
The chassis adds routes of its own outside this list: `/health`, `/auth/*`
and `/public/*`.

claims.statement: The address lookup spike is temporary and saves nothing: one search box sends anything shaped like a UK postcode as a postcode search and everything else as a free-text search, through the INS backend.
claims.quote:
The page has one search box. `detect-search-mode.js` sends anything
shaped like a UK postcode as `postcode=` and everything else as `find=`.
claims.note: Recorded from the docs this part reads; the spike's own files belong to another part.

claims.statement: The address lookup spike shows three gaps between the lookup's results and the address form: line 1 has to be composed, the lookup has no county, and its country is free text where the form wants a reference-data code.
